341 | // [FEATURE GUIDE] Spec 1.4.3 Function -- Feature Toggle Map for Compiler
342 | // ============================================================================
343 | // This section documents how each spec 1.4.3 feature maps to RTL code and
344 | // how the logic changes when the feature is enabled (ON) vs disabled (OFF).
345 | // Compiler software engineers can use this to split the code by feature.
346 | //
347 | // Parameter / macro          | Spec 1.4.3 #   | Feature name
348 | // ---------------------------+----------------+--------------------------------
349 | // (always on)                | 1. Read Op     | Read Operation
350 | // (always on)                | 2. Write Op    | Write Operation
351 | // RA[1:0] pin                | 3. Read assist | Read Assist (RA)
352 | // WA, WAT[1:0], WAV[1:0] pin | 4. Write assist| Write Assist (WA)
353 | // RT[4:0] pin                | 5. Read margin | Read Margin Tuning (RT)
354 | // WT[3:0] pin                | 6. Write margin| Write Margin Tuning (WT)
355 | // TEST pin, tcdt/ttons/...   | 7. Self Time   | Self Time Bypass (TEST mode)
356 | // BYP pin                    | (pin-only)     | Bypass (BYP) -- no functional logic
357 | // BWEB[N-1:0] pin            | 8. Bit Write   | Bit Write (BWEB)
358 | // EN_COLRED param, CRSLE/..  | 9. Col Redund  | Column Redundancy (CR)
359 | // CENTER_DECODE param        | (compiler opt) | Center Decode (CD) vs Side Decode (SD)
360 | // CM param                   | (compiler opt) | Column Mux (CM)
361 | // BK param                   | (compiler opt) | Banks (BK)
362 | //
363 | // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
364 | // Feature 1: Read Operation (always on, cannot be disabled)
365 | //   Spec: CEB=0, WEB=1 at CLK rising edge -> Q = mem[A]
366 | //   RTL:  Read path in memory_operator task, casez 2'b10 (line ~2150)
367 | //         Q_r <= Q_tmp with assign #(tcd) delay (line ~347)
368 | //   OFF:  Not applicable -- core function always present.
369 | //
370 | // Feature 2: Write Operation (always on, cannot be disabled)
371 | //   Spec: CEB=0, WEB=0 at CLK rising edge -> mem[A] = D
372 | //   RTL:  Write path in memory_operator task, casez 2'b00 (line ~2062)
373 | //   OFF:  Not applicable -- core function always present.
374 | //
375 | // Feature 3: Read Assist (RA) -- spec 1.4.3.3
376 | //   Spec: RA[1:0] != 2'b00 enables lower wordline voltage for read.
377 | //   Pin:  RA[1:0] (port, line 279)
378 | //   RTL:  Pin declared but NOT used functionally (analog/physical feature).
379 | //         Behavioral model: RA is a no-op; read timing/data unchanged.
380 | //   ON (RA != 0):  Pin exists, no behavioral effect. Compiler keeps pin.
381 | //   OFF (RA == 0): Pin may be tied to 2'b00. Compiler can remove pin.

387 | //   RTL:  Pins declared but NOT used functionally (analog/physical feature).
388 | //         Behavioral model: WA/WAT/WAV are no-ops; write timing/data unchanged.
389 | //   ON (WA=1):  Pins exist, no behavioral effect. Compiler keeps pins.
390 | //   OFF (WA=0): Pins may be tied low. Compiler can remove pins.
391 | //   Code to strip: port declarations WA, WAT[1:0], WAV[1:0] (lines 276-278).

395 | //   Spec: RT[4:0] provides speed/robustness settings. RT=5'b00000 = slowest.

397 | //   RTL:  Pin declared but NOT used functionally (analog/physical feature).

446 | // Feature 8: Bit Write (BWEB) -- spec 1.4.3.8
447 | //   Spec: BWEB[N-1:0] active low; BWEB[i]=0 -> write bit i; BWEB[i]=1 -> hold.
448 | //   Pin:  BWEB[N-1:0] (line 271)
449 | //   RTL:  BWEB used in write path of memory_operator (every `if (BWEB_eff[j] === 1'b0)`
450 | //         branch). BWEB setup/hold timing checks (tbws/tbwh, lines 235-236, ~1060).

453 | //         writable. BWEB=x/z -> mem[a][i]=x (hazard R11).

455 | //         `if (BWEB_eff[j] === 1'b0)` always true. Compiler can remove:
456 | //           - BWEB port, BWEB_buf, BWEB_eff
457 | //           - BWEB setup/hold timing checks (tbws/tbwh)

348 | // ---------------------------+----------------+--------------------------------

350 | // (always on)                | 2. Write Op    | Write Operation
